title: Common Knowledge Can Filter Nash Equilibria
body_html:
Common Knowledge Can Filter Nash Equilibria

MFoGT gives finite-game examples showing that Nash stability alone does not require players to know opponents' payoff functions. When payoffs and rationality are common knowledge, some Nash equilibria may be ruled out because a player can anticipate another player's best-response behavior.

The same section also gives an example where common knowledge and pre-play communication still do not remove an inefficient equilibrium without an additional principle such as Pareto dominance.
